html:
The Kokowarra were an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland country west of Cooktown, on the Cape York Peninsula in north Queensland. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them beyond their name and territory. Their country lay close to the Palmer River, and the gold rush there in the 1870s brought thousands of miners, many of them Chinese, along with police and cattlemen, into the land of all the peoples around. Neighbours on the map include the Guugu Yimithirr, the Mutumui and the Kuku Yalanji. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
